1979-465.24.statement:
On a closed oriented Riemannian four-manifold,
\[
\chi(M)=\frac1{32\pi^2}\int_M
\bigl(|\operatorname{Riem}|^2-4|\operatorname{Ric}|^2+R^2\bigr)\,d\operatorname{vol}.
\]
With curvature two-form matrix \(\Omega\),
\[
p_1(TM)=-\frac1{8\pi^2}\operatorname{tr}(\Omega\wedge\Omega)
\]
in the stated Chern--Weil convention.

1979-467.12.reconstruction: The nonlinear-graviton construction concerns complex geometry with self-dual curvature under additional constraints; it is not a solution for all real Lorentzian Einstein metrics.

1979-472.1.reconstruction: The source\textquotesingle s \(W\) is a generating functional. Its relation to an effective action requires a Legendre transform; connected functions and the effective action must be distinguished in the later argument.

1979-473.9.statement:
If \(I(c)\) has the same value \(I\) for every admissible slice parameter \(c\), then
\[
\frac{\int w(c)I(c)\,dc}{\int w(c)\,dc}=I,
\]
provided the denominator is nonzero and the integrals or their regularized meanings exist. Taking \(w=e^{i\Omega}\) gives a gauge-fixing action; normalization is still required for the stated independence.

1979-482.10.statement:
For traceless Hermitian generators of \(\mathfrak{su}(N)\) normalized by \(\operatorname{Tr}(T^aT^b)=\delta^{ab}\), completeness gives
\[
\sum_a(T^a)_{ij}(T^a)_{kl}
=\delta_{il}\delta_{jk}-N^{-1}\delta_{ij}\delta_{kl}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\sum_a\operatorname{Tr}(T^aUT^aV)
=\operatorname{Tr}U\operatorname{Tr}V-N^{-1}\operatorname{Tr}(UV).
\]
Adding the normalized identity generator gives the \(U(N)\) version without the subtraction.

1979-483.4.notes:
\ru{Теорема 1.1}: a unique bar-invariant element has the expansion
\[
C^{\prime}_w=q^{-\ell(w)/2}\sum_{y\le w}P_{y,w}T_y,
\]
with \(P_{w,w}=1\) and the strict degree bound (12).

1979-486.5.notes: After defining speciality, the recorder writes:\par\ru{Неизвестно: стратификация или клет. разбиение}.

1979-487.2.notes: The fragment\textquotesingle s central line reads:\par\ru{Элементу} \(G_{n,k}\) \ru{соотв. пара гиперсимплекс + конфигурация}.

1979-476.6.statement:
Fix \(x\in\mathbb P^1(\mathbb C)\). For generic quadruples, put
\[
c_x(g_0,g_1,g_2,g_3)
=D\bigl(\operatorname{cr}(g_0x,g_1x,g_2x,g_3x)\bigr).
\]
The five-term identity makes this a homogeneous measurable real three-cocycle for \(GL_2(\mathbb C)\), restricting to \(SL_2(\mathbb C)\). It represents the nonzero degree-three volume class under the comparison between measurable and continuous cohomology. Changing \(x\) gives a cohomologous cocycle.

1979-485.2.fate: \citet[Sec.~3 and the proof of Thm.~6]{olshanskii1980construction} supplies the Gaussian model and its compact dual; compare the decomposition under restriction in \citet[Sec.~1]{olshanskii1978unitary}. The result was formulated in the note presented in June 1979, so the talk is treated as contemporary exposition. The precise public release day of the 1980 issue remains unverified.

1979-465.21.statement:
For a nonnegative self-adjoint Laplace-type operator \(P\) on a closed smooth four-dimensional Riemannian manifold, form \(\zeta_P\) from its positive eigenvalues and let \(B_4\) denote the constant term in the integrated heat expansion. Then
\[
m=\zeta_P(0)=B_4-\dim\ker P.
\]
This value need not be an integer. For the scalar Laplacian on the unit round \(S^4\), the standard coefficient gives \(B_4=29/90\) and \(m=-61/90\), since the kernel consists of constants.
1979-465.21.reconstruction: \oursComputed\ For that sphere \(R=12\), \(|\operatorname{Ric}|^2=36\), \(|\operatorname{Riem}|^2=24\), and \(\operatorname{vol}=8\pi^2/3\). Substituting in \((360(4\pi)^2)^{-1}\int(5R^2-2|\operatorname{Ric}|^2+2|\operatorname{Riem}|^2)\) yields \(29/90\). An index supertrace may be integral even when individual regularized counts are not.

1979-466.4.statement: Over \(\mathbb C\), let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional vector space with nondegenerate alternating form \(\omega\), and let \(A:V\to V\) satisfy \(\omega(Au,v)=\omega(u,Av)\). There is a symplectic basis in which \(A=\operatorname{diag}(J,J^{\mathsf T})\), with \(J\) in Jordan normal form. Each Jordan block therefore occurs with its paired transpose.

1979-463.10.statement: \oursComputed\ For the printed expression and \(\omega(p,q)=-p^2+q^2\), take \(k_1=(1,0),k_2=(0,1),k_3=(0,0),k_4=(1,1)\). Both conservation laws hold and all denominators are nonzero, but the two fractions give \(1+1/5=6/5\), so the written vanishing claim is false.

1979-466.1.reconstruction: \ours\ The exact Fourier formula follows by differentiating in \(b\), integrating by parts to obtain \(I'=-bI/(2a)\), and using the Gaussian integral at \(b=0\). The first integral is positive but extraordinarily small; coarse oscillatory quadrature is unsuitable.

1979-466.2.reconstruction: \ours\ Termwise integration follows from domination by \(e^{-ax^4+|b||x|}\). The series converges for every finite \(b\). The value was checked independently by direct high-precision quadrature; the small scaled frequency makes this stable.

1979-466.3.reconstruction: \oursComputed\ The contributing saddles of \(-z^4+ibz\) are \(r e^{i\pi/6}\) and \(r e^{5i\pi/6}\). Shifting the real contour to height \(r/2\) makes their exponentially small contribution numerically accessible. The error is absolute inside the braces, not a uniform relative error near zeros of the cosine.

1979-470.11.reconstruction: \ours\ Indeed the multiplication algebra is maximal abelian, so \(\mathcal M'\subset L^\infty\subset\mathcal M\). Factoriality forces \(\mathcal M'=\mathbb C I\). A group-measure-space crossed product acts on a different Hilbert space and must not be substituted silently.

1979-463.1.fate: The contemporary definition and additive equation are in \citet[Sec.~1, pp.~192--193, eqs.~(1), (3)--(5)]{zakharovschulman1980degenerative}. The paper was received on 1 September 1979 and published in June 1980; receipt is not asserted to be a public circulation date. The later systematic formulation is \citet[Sec.~3, eqs.~(3.8)--(3.9)]{zakharovschulman1988invariants}.

1979-463.2.fate: The exact difference-curve parametrization appears in \citet[Sec.~1, p.~193, eqs.~(12)--(13)]{zakharovschulman1980degenerative}, published in June 1980. That paper credits the general example to S.~V.~Manakov, private communication. The arbitrary-function construction is written explicitly in \citet[Sec.~3, eqs.~(3.10)--(3.12)]{zakharovschulman1988invariants}, followed by the distinction between partial and complete degeneracy. The 1980 formula pages were read and visually checked in the original.

1979-463.6.fate: The kinetic form of the resonance obstruction was published soon after the seminar in \citet[Sec.~1, p.~195, final paragraph]{zakharovschulman1980degenerative}, excluding singular delta-type kinetic kernels. The general statement for analytic Hamiltonian invariants with a quadratic leading term is proved in \citet[Theorem~3.1, pp.~291--293]{zakharovschulman1988invariants}; its introduction, pp.~285--286, also identifies a brief 1985 announcement. Class A records the early kinetic result; the full modern reconstruction is supported by the later theorem.

GP-1975-10.title: Continuum confinement and the static potential
GP-1975-10.statement:
For four-dimensional continuum pure \(SU(N)\) Yang--Mills theory at zero temperature, with fixed finite \(N\ge2\) and external fundamental static sources, establish a well-defined subtracted static potential with positive asymptotic string tension:
\[
\lim_{r\to\infty}\frac{V(r)}r=\tau>0.
\]
There are no dynamical fundamental quarks in this formulation. Occurrence 1979-480.3 specializes to \(SU(3)\). Occurrence 1979-482.14 returns to the general confinement goal and proposes normalized large-rank loop equations as a route; that limiting method is not identified with the fixed-rank statement. The stronger constant-width flux-tube hypothesis is excluded from this problem identity.
GP-1975-10.status: As of 10 November 2026, the verified results are partial. Wilson's strong-coupling lattice area law \citep[Secs.~IV and VI]{wilson1974confinement} and the controlled large-rank lattice expansion \citep[Theorem~3.1 and Corollaries~3.2--3.3]{chatterjee2015string} do not provide the asserted continuum proof. With light dynamical quarks, string breaking changes the asymptotic static-energy question \citep[Sec.~4]{bulava2019string}. The continuum existence-and-mass-gap problem and confinement are separately stated in \citet[Sec.~5]{jaffewitten2000yangmills}; the former is still listed as unsolved by \citet{clay2026yangmills}. The reused older identifier follows the static-potential goal, while the distinct proposed methods and physical regimes remain explicit.
